history.summary: CORRECTED TOWN: the temple is in Sitamai village, about 19 km from Nilokheri on the alternative Karnal-Kaithal route, not in Karnal city. It is an ancient brick temple said to be perhaps the only temple in India solely dedicated to Goddess Sita, consort of Rama. Local belief holds it marks the spot where Mother Earth split open to receive Sita in proof of her sinlessness. The temple was already documented in Denzil Ibbetson's 1883 settlement report of the Panipat tahsil and Karnal parganah, so it predates 1883; its ornamented brick shrine has deep line patterns said to have been cut into the bricks before firing. Local accounts say the shrine was destroyed by Mughal invaders and its bricks recovered from a tank and reassembled by the people (verify). The temple is under the administration of the Ramanandi Bairagis.

name: Sitamai Temple
town_description: Sitamai is a village in Karnal district of Haryana, about 19 km from Nilokheri on an alternative route between Karnal and Kaithal. It is a small rural settlement set in the fertile agricultural belt of eastern Haryana, known almost entirely for its ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Sita. The village draws pilgrims rather than tourists, and retains a quiet agrarian character.
